subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway memory pressure silently kills all tool responses — degraded state before OOM

question: After sustained critical memory pressure, should the gateway visibly reject new work and gracefully restart, visibly fail work without restarting, or remain diagnostics-only?
rationale: Automatic recovery can interrupt active work, while warning-only behavior leaves channel users blocked with no in-product recovery path; source evidence cannot choose that lifecycle policy.

options.title: Visible load shed and restart
options.body: Reject new turns with a clear degraded-state response, drain active work safely, and restart after sustained critical pressure.

options.title: Visible failures without restart
options.body: Return explicit tool and lane errors while keeping the gateway alive for operator-directed recovery.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Retain warning and snapshot behavior and leave restart policy entirely to operators.

recommendation.title: Visible load shed and restart
recommendation.body: Reject new turns with a clear degraded-state response, drain active work safely, and restart after sustained critical pressure.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available history-based candidate connected to both current pressure diagnostics and embedded-run lifecycle safeguards.
